extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies, regulated sources, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Reviewing and evaluating a state's SIP revision and redesignation request to demonstrate that an SO2 nonattainment area meets statutory and regulatory requirements for redesignation to attainment and that the accompanying maintenance plan is approvable under the CAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (1) — Determination that the applicable NAAQS has been attained
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(i) requires that the EPA determine if a nonattainment area has attained the applicable NAAQS in order to redesignate the area to attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA may consider air quality monitoring data and air quality modeling data (2014 SO2 Guidance). For the 2010 1-hour SO2 NAAQS, a monitoring-based attainment determination relies on design values; modeling may be needed where monitors are not located in areas of maximum concentration. The submission should show monitoring and/or modeling support for attainment, and demonstrate that controls relied upon in modeling are implemented and representative of source characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (2) — State has a fully approved SIP under CAA section 110(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(ii) requires that the EPA fully approve the applicable implementation plan for the area under CAA section 110(k) in order to redesignate that area to attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A redesignation cannot proceed if a required SIP element is disapproved, subject to a finding of failure to submit, or only partially/conditionally/limitedly approved. The SIP must include required elements (e.g., emissions inventory, control strategy, modeling demonstration, RACM/RACT analysis, RFP analysis, contingency measures, NNSR regulations) and those elements must be EPA-approved for purposes of redesignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (3) — Air quality improvement due to permanent and enforceable reductions in emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(iii) requires EPA to determine that the air quality improvement is due to permanent and enforceable reductions in emissions from implementation of the SIP, applicable Federal regulations, and other permanent and enforceable reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent and enforceable measures include SIP-approved emission limits embedded in permits and federally enforceable control measures; source shutdowns count if reflected in the SIP and permits are modified accordingly. The submission should document the implemented permanent controls, emission reductions (quantified), permit changes, and any non-transfer of emission reduction credits that would undermine permanence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (4) — Area has a fully approved maintenance plan pursuant to CAA section 175A
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(iv) requires that the area has a fully approved maintenance plan under section 175A of the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under section 175A the maintenance plan must demonstrate continued attainment for at least 10 years after redesignation; the State must submit a revised maintenance plan 8 years after redesignation demonstrating maintenance for an additional 10 years. The Calcagni Memo further explains maintenance-plan content (see five specific maintenance-plan elements). EPA evaluates whether the plan meets the statutory requirements and guidance to approve it as a SIP revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion (5) — State has met all applicable requirements under section 110 and part D of title I of the CAA
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA section 107(d)(3)(E)(v) requires that the State has met all applicable requirements for the area under section 110 and part D of Title I of the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses whether the area has satisfied section 110 general requirements and Part D requirements (subpart 1: sections 172(c), 173, 175A, 176, 179; subpart 5 for SO2: sections 191 and 192). An area cannot be redesignated if any applicable requirement remains unmet. For SO2, transportation conformity SIPs are not required because the conformity provisions historically did not apply to SO2 (transportation conformity rules do not apply to SO2 for the Allegheny County NAA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance plan element — Attainment emissions inventory (attainment inventory)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a maintenance plan, states are required to submit an emissions inventory to identify the level of emissions in the area which is sufficient to attain and maintain the SO2 NAAQS (the attainment inventory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attainment year is generally a year within the attaining design value period; the State must justify the selected attainment year if different (e.g., 2017 selected here because of NEI availability and atypical emissions in other years). Inventory methods: use point/area source emissions from the NEI with corrections as needed; verify point source emissions against EPA EIS; estimate area sources proportionally; use MOVES (MOVES3) for mobile sources; include natural sources (fires/biogenics) as appropriate. Projection inventories (e.g., 2026, 2035) are developed from the attainment inventory using growth factors and adjusted for implemented enforceable controls or shutdowns; point sources with implemented enforceable controls/shutdowns should be excluded from projections as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance plan element — Maintenance demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Calcagni Memo describes two ways for a State to demonstrate maintenance for at least 10 years: (1) show future emissions will not exceed the attainment inventory level, or (2) model to show that the future mix of sources and emission rates will not cause a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may demonstrate maintenance via projected emissions inventories that remain below the attainment inventory (as Pennsylvania did for 2026 and 2035), or via future-case air quality modeling showing no violations. Projections should account for implemented controls, shutdowns, and permitted future sources (with justification if a permitted facility is later terminated). Use consistent corrections and modeling inputs across base and projection years; document assumptions and data sources (growth factors, EIA outlook, employment forecasts, FAA forecasts, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance plan element — Continued operation of a monitoring network (40 CFR part 58)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Calcagni Memo and 2014 SO2 Guidance indicate that once an area has been redesignated to attainment, the state should continue to operate an appropriate air quality monitoring network as provided under 40 CFR part 58 to verify attainment status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state/air agency must commit to continued operation of monitors, submit annual monitoring network plans to EPA per 40 CFR 58.10, and make no changes to the network without EPA pre-approval. Monitoring serves as the primary verification for continued attainment and as the triggering mechanism for contingency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance plan element — Verification of continued attainment (legal authority & tracking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2014 SO2 Guidance states each air agency should ensure it has the legal authority to implement and enforce all measures necessary to attain and maintain the SO2 NAAQS and indicate how it will track progress of the maintenance plan via monitoring or modeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submittal should demonstrate legal authority (e.g., ACHD Article XXI) and an integrated approach to track progress using monitoring data and emissions inventories (annual point-source inventories and triennial PADEP area/mobile inventories). Monitored concentrations are the primary trigger for contingency measures; emissions inventories inform assessments but are not appropriate triggers because of meteorological effects and reporting lag. New source review should require modeling showing new/modified major sources will not cause or contribute to violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance plan element — Contingency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 175A(d) requires that a maintenance plan include such contingency measures as the EPA deems necessary to assure that the State will promptly correct a violation of the NAAQS that occurs after redesignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maintenance plan should identify the contingency measures to be adopted, provide a schedule and procedure for adoption and implementation, and include a time limit for the State to act. The plan should specify how contingency measures are triggered (monitoring-based triggers are appropriate) and the mechanisms/timelines to implement measures to correct any violation promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air quality monitoring data completeness requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Data completeness rules for monitoring required to validate design values and monitor-based determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A year meets data completeness when all four quarters are complete. A quarter is complete when at least 75 percent of the sampling days have complete data. A sampling day has complete data if 75 percent of the hourly concentration values, including State-flagged data affected by approved exceptional events for exclusion, are reported. Design values are valid if they encompass three consecutive calendar years of complete data.

rubrics_metrics.name: SO2 design value calculation and criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: How to calculate the design value for the 2010 1-hour SO2 NAAQS and the numeric standard to meet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 40 CFR part 50 and appendix T, the 2010 1-hour SO2 NAAQS is met at a monitoring site when the 3-year average of the annual 99th percentile of daily maximum 1-hour average concentrations is less than or equal to 75 ppb, using the rounding convention in appendix T. A design value is valid when based on three consecutive calendar years of complete data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of attainment-plan modeling vs. actual-emissions modeling for redesignation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA may rely on attainment-plan modeling based on allowable emission limits if source characteristics remain reasonably represented; otherwise, actual-emissions-based modeling may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per the 2014 SO2 Guidance, attainment demonstration modeling submitted in an earlier SIP may support a redesignation if the modeled control strategy has been fully implemented and source characteristics are still reasonably represented. If monitoring sites are not located at concentrations of maximum impact, additional modeling may be necessary to estimate concentrations throughout the area. The state should document that sources are meeting allowable limits used in the modeling and that controls relied upon were implemented.
